key_insight: Inherited microsegregation and short-range diffusion create Cu-rich regions that melt locally at 1100 °C, below the alloy’s predicted global solid-state stability limit of 1260 °C.
engineering_relevance: SPS processing windows for Cu–Ni–Ti–Zr–Hf powders should account for local composition-dependent solidus temperatures, not just bulk equilibrium predictions.
method: Induction melting and atomization of Cu15Ni35Ti25Zr12.5Hf12.5, followed by SPS at 850–1100 °C.
2D local-equilibrium heat maps to assess segregation-driven melting.
evidence_signal: Localized melting at 1100 °C, Cu enrichment up to approximately 41 at. %, and Cu–Hf co-segregation after solidification support the proposed mechanism.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify diffusion kinetics or validate the mechanism beyond this alloy and processing range.
paper_title: Early-stage local melting during solid-state sintering of a Cu-Ni-Ti-Zr-Hf alloy: A combined thermodynamic and kinetic analysis
